messages:
support-ops: Heads up — customer acme-prod reports a sudden vectors/sec drop starting ~2026-03-17T03:00Z. tokens/sec looks steady, embeddings are timing out or 500ing. trace=tr_8b2f

alex: On it. Do we have an example request payload and model id?

support-ops: Example: POST /v1/embeddings model=embed-redwood-14 batch_size=64. payload small arrays, dims look correct on client side. Received errors: 500 x 120, 429 x 40 over 10m.

maria: Can you paste a server-side log snippet for a failing request? any GPU OOMs?

support-ops: Log snippet attached below:
```
[03:05:12Z] request_id=tr_8b2f status=500 model=embed-redwood-14 batch=64 queue_len=92 gpu_waiters=88 kvcache_hit=false error="batching timeout"
[03:05:12Z] stack=runtime: batch window expired, flush triggered
[03:05:13Z] gpu0: util=96% mem=72% waiting=12
```

maria: Hmm queue_len ~92 and gpu_waiters high. Token path still reporting tokens/sec ~normal?

jon: Could be KV cache thrashing — embeddings generate many unique prefixes so kvcache miss rate went up, causing longer GPU compute. Check kvcache eviction stats and model variant fallback.

sarah-ml: Also check if batching window config changed in rollout last night. A smaller max-batch or larger window could affect throughput balance between tokens and vectors.

alex: Repro steps request from support-ops: 1) curl example with header x-customer=acme-prod 2) use parallel runner to send 1000 small embedding requests at QPS 80 3) collect /metrics and /debug/kvcache

support-ops: Repro command we used:
```
seq 1 1000 | xargs -n1 -P80 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" -d '{"model":"embed-redwood-14","input":"test string"}'
```
We saw that client-observed tokens/sec ~6000, vectors/sec ~150 (expected ~1200).

maria: That gap is big. Two hypotheses: (1) GPU saturation causing single-request latency blowup (vectors/sec drops), (2) batching degenerated into many small batches due to a change in batcher scheduling.

jon: Quick check — can eng-infra drop a snapshot of batcher histograms? need distribution of batch sizes over the period. @sre-bot can you dump /metrics?

sre-bot: metrics snapshot posted to #infra-monitoring link: https://internal/metrics/snapshots/4098761234

alex: From metrics: p50 batch_size=2, p90=4, p99=16, avg_latency_per_embedding=420ms (was ~120ms baseline). Also GPU queue depth ~96 sustained.

sarah-ml: p50 batch_size=2 explains vectors/sec collapse — continuous small batches are extremely inefficient. Why did batcher fail to accumulate? look for recent commit touching batching/window or rate limiter config.

maria: Rollout log shows a config push at 02:45Z that changed "batch_window_ms" from 12 -> 3 for embed-redwood-14 (intended to reduce latency). That would reduce batch sizes dramatically.

alex: That matches. Smaller window -> smaller batch sizes -> more overhead -> GPU queue still high due to many tiny kernels. Need to revert or apply adaptive batching.

jon: Temporary mitigation: revert batch_window_ms to 12 for embed-redwood-14 and enable quick kv_prefetch experiment. I'll open a rollback PR.

support-ops: Customer impact: degraded throughput, some 500s/429s. ETA to mitigations?

jon: Rolling config revert to prod region A in 2m, then region B. I'll watch metrics.

sre-bot: Config rollback started: cfg_revert_4098761234 by jon @ 03:23:10Z

alex: Meanwhile, collect a short-term workaround for customers — suggest increasing client-side batch_size to 128 (if they can), or switch to dedicated capacity if critical. Also provide a status note to acme support.

maria: Post-rollback checks: batch_size p50 jumps to 24 within 90s, avg_latency_per_embedding drops to 140ms, GPU util stabilizes to 78%.

sre-bot: Post-rollback metrics: vectors/sec returning to baseline within 3m. 500 errors dropping to normal.

support-ops: Notified acme-prod: "We identified a batching config regression from a recent rollout; we've reverted it and are monitoring. Please let us know if you still see slowdowns."

alex: Follow-ups: (1) add canary gating for batch_window changes (2) add a regression alert for tokens/sec vs vectors/sec divergence >3x (3) postmortem and change review. Assign to eng-ml + eng-sre.

jon: I'll create the canary ticket and alert rule. maria to draft postmortem.

maria: Will do. I'll include repro commands, logs, and timeline.

support-ops: Closing loop with customer once we hit 30m of healthy metrics. Thanks team :thumbsup:
